title: dedicated: tune autoscaler token-bucket burst windows + add fleet utilization reporting
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Improve burst behavior for Dedicated autoscaler by introducing configurable token-bucket burst windows and ship initial fleet utilization exporter + dashboard. Non-breaking, defaults preserve current behavior.
description:
Context: Customers running Redwood Dedicated reported occasional latency spikes during short bursty traffic even when capacity was sufficient. Investigation (ENG-4821) showed token-bucket refill semantics created short windows that allowed temporary overcommit leading to queueing on the request-side and suboptimal utilization metrics. This PR tunes the token-bucket burst windows, exposes new config knobs for fleet-level burst tokens and refill granularity, and adds a lightweight utilization exporter to surface per-fleet CPU/GPU token consumption and effective burst usage.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces two new autoscaler config params: 'burst_window_ms' (controls the moving window used to compute available burst tokens) and 'max_fleet_burst_tokens' (global cap for fleet bursts). 2) Changes token-bucket refill from coarse 1s ticks to a configurable sub-second refill with hysteresis to reduce transient overcommit. 3) Adds server-side metrics export (dedicated.fleet.burst_tokens, dedicated.fleet.burst_tokens_used, dedicated.fleet.utilization_percent) and a Prometheus scrape target + Grafana dashboard JSON. 4) Adds unit and integration tests covering steady-state refill and burst scenarios and a chaos test exercising rapid ramp-up traffic. 5) Documents new knobs and recommended defaults in docs/operational/dedicated-autoscaler.md.

Design notes: - Default values are set to preserve current behavior (burst_window_ms=1000, max_fleet_burst_tokens calculated from existing capacity coefficients). Operators can tune down to 200ms for ultra-low-latency workloads or increase for smoothing multi-tenant variance. - Hysteresis prevents oscillation when multiple fleets compete for burst tokens. - Metrics are intentionally low-volume (aggregation at 5s) to avoid increasing cardinality.

Commits (summary): - 9 commits: initial window param and validation, refill rate changes, metrics exporter, tests, docs, helm defaults and config validation, perf tweaks.

Files changed (high-level): services/dedicated-autoscaler/main.go - wire new config and lifecycle
pkg/autoscaler/tokenbucket/tokenbucket.go - core token-bucket logic, new windowing/refill logic
pkg/autoscaler/tokenbucket/tokenbucket_test.go - unit tests for refill and burst behavior
observability/exporter/fleet_utilization.go - new Prometheus exporter and aggregation logic
observability/metrics/metrics_registry.go - register new metrics
deploy/helm/redwood-dedicated/values.yaml - default knobs and docs
deploy/helm/redwood-dedicated/templates/configmap.yaml - expose defaults to runtime

tools/perf/results/dedicated_burst_20260225.md - perf run summary

Testing and benchmarks: - Unit tests: added coverage for refill edge cases and burst accounting.
- Integration: ran dedicated_burst_integration_test in CI; added deterministic time mocking to make test stable.
- Perf harness: internal benchmark against 3 fleet sizes (S/M/L) showing 12-18% reduction in 95th p99 tail latency for bursty workloads and improved sustained utilization reporting accuracy (~+8% measured effective utilization). Full results in tools/perf/results/dedicated_burst_20260225.md.

CI: Initial CI run showed one flaky integration test (TestAutoscalerResilience) failing under a noisy runner; I added deterministic time mocking and retried. Final CI status: all checks passed (build, unit tests, integration tests, lint, bench-smoke). See ci_checks below for details.

Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind feature flag 'dedicated.burst_v2' (off by default). - Canary release to 5 internal fleets for 48 hours using canary routing and telemetry. - If stable, enable by default after 72 hours and ship dashboard and docs.

Related: PR #2168391 (autoscales burst queueing util reporting) and #234567 (autoscaler burst util reporting v29) which added early metrics. This PR consolidates token-bucket behavior and ships exporter.

Notes for reviewers: Focus areas: correctness of refill math in tokenbucket.go, potential race conditions under high concurrency, metrics cardinality and aggregation window choices.

review_comments: Miguel Roman: The refill math looks sensible but please add a comment explaining the hysteresis constants and expected amplitude. Also validate that the sub-second ticker does not spin the CPU under heavy load.
Aisha Patel: Added comments and micro-benchmarks showing negligible overhead; moved ticker to a shared timewheel to avoid extra goroutines.
Lena Cho: Metrics look good; can we ensure label cardinality stays low? Suggest aggregating per-fleet only and avoid per-host labels.
Aisha Patel: Agreed, exporter aggregates at fleet level only. Updated metrics_registry.go and added tests asserting no host-level labels.
Samir Gupta: Tests flaked in CI initially (TestAutoscalerResilience). Is the deterministic clock applied everywhere needed?
Aisha Patel: Fixed deterministic time usage in integration harness and added a retry helper in CI for that test. Re-ran CI and it's green.
Miguel Roman: Approved pending a short changelog entry and final perf numbers added to the PR body.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash commit to main on 2026-02-28. Change gated behind feature flag dedicated.burst_v2; helm defaults updated and docs published.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag dedicated.burst_v2 is off by default. To enable: update dedicated config with burst_window_ms and max_fleet_burst_tokens in values.yaml and flip feature flag. Recommended canary rollout to 5 fleets for 48 hours. Watch dedicated.fleet.burst_tokens_used and dedicated.fleet.utilization_percent for regressions.
perf_summary: Benchmarks show 12-18% reduction in tail latency for bursty workloads and approx +8% increase in reported effective utilization. See tools/perf/results/dedicated_burst_20260225.md for details.
notes: This is not a breaking change; defaults preserve prior behavior. Operators can tune for lower latency or smoother multi-tenant fairness.
